coordinatorReview.boundary: UI/internal labels classify located routing evidence, not proof of all field semantics. Zero unclassified rows does not mean zero uncertainty. Inherited180 rows are not independently type-resolved or behaviorally accepted. Corrected keybindings authority is the file-backed service, not proof the legacy GlobalSettings field is unused or safe to remove.

scope: Resolves all 214 canonical GlobalSettings fields (declaration order per parity-settings-properties.json) to a classification of ui-consumer vs internal-authority, built by reusing the accepted properties/consumers/unobserved/persistence JSON without rescanning the whole tree, plus a targeted direct-name grep of src/renderer/src for fields the GlobalSettings-token-prefilter in parity-settings-consumers.json missed (files that consume a field via a narrower local prop/hook type, never importing the raw GlobalSettings type, so never entered that scan's 472-file candidate set). No field mapping in this document is a claim of full behavioral/UI-parity closure; SP01-SP13 and the 10 reviewed unobserved-cohort traces are reused by reference, not repeated.

method.primaryClassification: For each field, non-test references (paths not matching *.test.ts(x), *.spec.ts, test-fixtures/test-harness/fixtures files) from parity-settings-consumers.json were partitioned into src/renderer/src/components/**, other src/renderer/src/**, and src/main|src/shared. A field with any non-test renderer reference is ui-consumer; a field with only main/shared non-test references is internal-authority. Test/fixture-only reference sets are not treated as consumer evidence (per task instruction) and would fall back to prefilter-miss verification below.
method.unobservedCohort: The 10 fields with referenceStatus no-observed-reference in parity-settings-consumers.json are classified from the reviewed narrative in parity-settings-unobserved-contracts.md (coordinator-verified bounded contracts), not re-derived, then cross-checked against the same direct-name grep as every other field.
method.prefilterMissTrace: For every field left internal-authority (or in the unobserved cohort) after the primary pass, ran `grep -rn '\b<field>\b' src/renderer/src` (non-test) against the frozen source at c97906287bb7a390b25e2025b600d9fb3c25d9c3 to find renderer consumers invisible to the GlobalSettings-token scan. The initial26 direct-name candidates were inspected;25 have genuine settings-shaped reads/writes and keybindings was corrected to dedicated internal authority (basis prefilter-miss-verified, cited anchor is the directly-grepped file:line, read at that location, not assumed from the grep alone). 4 additional fields (terminalCursorStyleDefaultedToBlock, autoRenameBranchFromWorkDefaultedOn, terminalAllowOsc52ClipboardDefaultedOnForAllUsers, rightSidebarOpenByDefault) surfaced only in src/renderer/src/web/preload-api/web-preferences-store.ts or web-settings-api.ts, a web-build defaults-mirror, not a rendered settings control; these stay internal-authority with the pointer recorded, not silently dropped.

closureClaim: NONE. This is field-routing classification evidence only; per-field UI behavior, persistence execution and original test parity remain open per AGENTS.md gate.

CORRECTED: prior citation App.tsx:29 was a false positive — that line is `import { useGlobalKeybindings } from './app-shell/use-global-keybindings'`, a substring match on the relative import path string, not a GlobalSettings.keybindings read. Re-inspected renderer store slice ShortcutsPane.tsx:58/use-settings-store-model.ts:36 (`useAppStore((state) => state.keybindings)`): this reads a same-named but DIFFERENT renderer store slice (KeybindingsSlice, src/renderer/src/store/slices/keybindings.ts:12, type KeybindingOverrides) populated via `window.api.keybindings.*` IPC calls to the dedicated KeybindingService/keybinding-file.ts system, not via GlobalSettings persistence. Also re-inspected browser-manager-bindings.ts:36/58 `this.settingsResolver?.().keybindings`: settingsResolver is set at main-process-account-services.ts:121 to `() => ({ keybindings: state.keybindings?.getOverrides() })`, where `state.keybindings` is main-process-state.ts:89's `KeybindingService | null` field — again the file-backed service, not GlobalSettings.keybindings. Both are genuine field-name collisions with the declared GlobalSettings.keybindings (KeybindingOverrides, no builder default, src/shared/global-settings-types.ts:272). No code path reading/writing GlobalSettings.keybindings itself through the settings load/save pipeline was found in this bounded trace, consistent with the original scanner's no-observed-reference result and the reviewed unobserved-contracts.md narrative (dedicated file/service drives current bindings, independent of generic settings persistence). Classified internal-authority as a dedicated non-settings-pipeline authority binding, not forced to ui-consumer.
